sebelum.title: Before Prophethood
sebelum.intro: The first forty years before being commissioned as the Messenger of Allah. Al-Mubarakfuri notes this period as the formation of noble character, trustworthiness (al-Amin), and divine protection from pre-Islamic ignorance.

items.d: On Monday, Rabi'ul Awwal, in the Year of the Elephant. Born orphaned; his grandfather named him Muhammad — a name uncommon among Arabs at the time.
After being nursed by Tsuwaibah for a few days, he was raised by Halimah as-Sa'diyah in the desert. The blessings experienced by Halimah's family led them to keep him longer than customary.
Two angels visited him while playing, opened his chest, and purified his heart. This event prompted Halimah to return him to his mother.
Aminah passed away on the return journey from visiting Yatsrib. Ummu Aiman brought him back to Makkah.

items.t: Grandfather's Passing & Custody to Abu Talib
items.d: Abdul Muttalib entrusted Abu Talib with his care — a guardianship that extended into protection for over forty years.

items.t: Journey to Sham & Bahira the Monk
items.d: Joined his uncle's trade caravan. In Busra, the monk Bahira recognized the signs of prophethood and advised Abu Talib to take him home for safety.
Inter-tribal conflict during sacred months. His role was supporting his uncles by gathering arrows.
A pact established at the house of Abdullah bin Jud'an to defend anyone wronged in Makkah. After prophethood, he stated he would still uphold it if called upon.
Managed Khadijah's trade merchandise to Sham accompanied by Maisarah. Maisarah's account of his honesty and noble character initiated Khadijah's interest.
Khadijah was forty years old and the most noble woman in her society — in lineage, wealth, and intellect. His dowry was twenty young camels.
When tribes nearly went to war over placing the Black Stone, he spread his cloak and asked each tribal leader to hold an edge together.
As forty approached, his inclination for solitude grew stronger, especially during Ramadan — leading up to the first revelation.

hijrah.title: Migration to Madinah
hijrah.intro: The defining historical event marking the beginning of the Hijri calendar. Meticulous strategy, strict confidentiality, and divine help altered the course of history from vulnerability in Makkah to a new center of civilization.

items.d: Quraysh leaders agreed to pick a young warrior from each tribe to strike the Prophet together, preventing Bani Hashim from taking revenge against all tribes.
Ali bin Abu Talib slept covered in the Prophet's bed, tasked with returning goods entrusted to the Prophet by Makkans.
He walked past the surrounders unnoticed, proceeding to the house of Abu Bakr.
Heading south — opposite to Madinah — to mislead pursuers. Quraysh posted a 100-camel reward for capturing either of them.
Abdullah bin Abu Bakr brought city news, Asma' bint Abu Bakr delivered provisions — earning her title Dzatun Nithaqain — and Amir bin Fuhairah grazed sheep to erase footprints and supply milk.
Abdullah bin Uraiqith, still adhering to his people's faith, was hired as a guide for his mastery of desert paths — a tactical decision demonstrating professionalism.
Bounty hunter who nearly caught up, but his horse repeatedly stumbled. He returned with a guarantee of safety from the Prophet — and later embraced Islam.
Stayed four days and built Quba' Mosque, the first mosque founded upon piety.
En route to the city center, he performed the first Friday prayer in the settlement of Bani Salim bin Auf.
He allowed his camel to walk freely so no tribe felt bypassed. It stopped on land owned by orphans Sahl and Suhail — later purchased for Al-Masjid an-Nabawi.

items.t: Three Foundations of a New Society
items.d: Building Al-Masjid an-Nabawi as the center, establishing brotherhood between Muhajirun and Ansar, and drafting the written charter governing Madinah's inhabitants including Jewish tribes.

wafat.title: Passing of the Prophet ﷺ
wafat.intro: The final days of the greatest human after completing the delivery of the divine message over twenty-three years. The most poignant moment for the Companions, testing the firmness of their faith.

items.t: Signals of Farewell at Farewell Pilgrimage
items.d: In his sermon at Arafat, he called upon the people to bear witness that the message had been delivered, speaking words perceived by many as a farewell.
After visiting Baqi' one night, he experienced a severe headache accompanied by high fever. The illness lasted about eleven days.
He requested permission from his wives to be nursed in Aishah's room, and they agreed. He was supported as he moved.

items.t: Abu Bakr Appointed to Lead Prayers
items.d: His fever worsened. When Aishah repeatedly requested the duty be transferred, he firmly instructed Abu Bakr to lead the prayer.
Including the counsel that no one should pass except having good expectations of Allah, and reminders regarding prayer and kindness to servants.
His pain temporarily eased. Supported by two men, he came out and sat on the left of Abu Bakar; Abu Bakr followed his prayer and amplified takbir.
He freed two servants, gave away remaining dinars in charity, and donated his weapons to the Muslims. His armor was pledged to a Jewish trader for grain.
As Muslims prepared for Fajr prayer, he lifted the room curtain, smiled watching them lined up in prayer. Abu Bakr thought he was stepping out to lead — many thought it signaled recovery.
He passed away in the forenoon of Monday, 12 Rabi'ul Awwal 11 AH, in Aishah's lap, at age sixty-three. His final audible words were a supplication to be with ar-Rafiq al-A'la — the Supreme Companion.
Following the principle that prophets are buried where they pass, the grave was dug by Abu Talhah in Aishah's room. Burial took place on Tuesday night.
